text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT TENDER - Egypt's official commodities buyer was seeking 50,000 tonnes of soft red wheat from France for loading Dec 16-31. The deadline for receiving bids was 0900 local time (0700 GMT) on Nov 15. Bids are valid until Nov 18. Egypt was also seeking 50,000 tonnes of soft white Australian wheat for Dec 11-31 arrival and 100,000 tonnes of Argentinian wheat by Friday for loading from Dec 12-31.
WHEAT TENDER - Pakistan is likely to tender for at least 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat in a about a week's time, a Ministry of Food and Agriculture official said.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC said it was tendering Nov 13 for up to 80,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat, ordinary protein, for Bangladesh. Shipment was for Dec 1-25, 1996.

VEGOIL TENDER - Egypt seeks up to 35,000 T edible oils for first half January; 10,000 to 15,000 T crude sunflower oil or semi-refined cottonseed oil or U.S. cottonseed oil grade 162, 5,000 to 10,000 T degummed soyoil, any origin and 10,000 tonnes of palm oil of Malaysian or Indonesian origin.

LENTIL TENDER - CCC said it was seeking 900 tonnes of lentils for export to Iraq. Offers should be submitted by November 18 for reply the next day. Shipment was slated for Dec 6-20. Offers will be accepted to Jacintoport, Texas only.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwanese buyers are expected to tender for up to 26,000 tonnes of corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans this week, traders said. Taiwan Sugar Corp is seeking 10,000 tonnes of No.2 yellow corn with delivery date set during the tender. Taiwan's Hui Shung Group was expected to tender this week for 16,000 tonnes of corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans for March delivery.

RICE TENDER - Costa Rica will be seeking 46,000 tonnes of U.S. long grain paddy rice on November 13 , U.S. exporters said. The deal includes two shipments of 23,000 tonnes each. One lot was slated for February 24-March 4 arrival and another lot was set for April 1-8.

MARKET TALK - The Philippines is expected to increase corn imports from this year's 400,000 tonnes to one million tonnes annually up to the year 2000, experts said. The projected increase could be attributed to the low use of high-quality corn seeds by domestic farmers, University of the Philippines Integrated Plant Breeding deputy director Manuel Logrono said.

... South Korean feed processors are expected to buy more than 200,000 tonnes of Canadian feed wheat by December to cover their needs for February/March shipment. Feed wheat prices currently appear more attractive than corn prices, traders said.

... Canadian and Australian sales of malting barley to China could be limited by weather woes and disease concerns, which are cutting the amount of quality grain available for export this year, industry sources said. Canada was hit by early snow that damaged the barley crop and would keep sales to China of the higher quality malting variety below 300,000 tonnes, a Canadian marketing source said. Canada had already sold close to 300,000 tonnes of malting barley to China in the current marketing year (August-July), he said.
